notes: Baseline: the dataset's own system prompt, one call, no extra instructions.

Same extract-then-solve split as the overlap evidence demands (overlap is the dominant failure on all three splits), but with a general preference language (windows, avoid-windows, ordering, adjacency, gaps, early/late) that the solver maximises by largest-satisfiable-subset search. Motivation: future evals add unseen preference types, so the representation should cover relational/negative wishes, not just the four prefer_window phrases seen in ood_dev.

Parent fails mostly on overlaps (dev_in 47/58, dev_v2 42/63, ood 19/43) and window/at/before slips, i.e. the 8B model cannot place events itself. Replaced the single call with an LLM that only extracts the current event set + hard constraints + preferences (as prefer_window) into JSON, and an exact sequence solver tool that places events (5-min grid for v2 times like 2:20pm/12:05pm) maximising satisfied preferences; it always emits a full JSON list, fixing no_json chit-chat turns too.

Extract-then-solve (exact solver removes the dominant overlap failures) plus a second LLM pass that audits the extraction against the full transcript before solving. Motivated by multi-turn state errors in the evidence (dev_v2 extra_event x8 after "revert to Turn 4", constraints that must persist across turns, at/before slips); the solver reads the reviewer's JSON and falls back to the extractor's if the review is unparseable. Tests whether buying a verification call is worth the extra tokens.

Cheapest hypothesis: same single call, but the empty prompt is replaced by an explicit procedure. Evidence: overlaps dominate every split and come from re-placing untouched events; ood 'violates_before' x6 shows the model reads 'before X' as start<X (it means end<=X); no_json x4 are chit-chat turns where the model answered in prose/an object; dev_v2 extra_event x8 after 'revert to Turn N'. The prompt says: start from the last calendar, keep times, list busy intervals and drop the new event into a free gap, defines at/before/after/between, gives a generic soft-preference vocabulary, and always outputs the full list.

Stacks both fixes: the procedural prompt of c2 (keep previous times, end-by semantics for 'before', always full list) plus a preference-aware version of c1's zero-token repair tool. The tool also parses soft wishes per event (sentences with 'ideally'/'suits me'/'around'...; time-of-day vocabulary taking the LAST phrase, so 'mornings are busy, so ... afternoon' maps to afternoon; soft clock phrases like 'ideally before 2pm' become windows) and, even when the LLM's calendar is valid, moves events whose hard constraint is known into their preferred window when that keeps everything legal. With oracle constraints it met 23/24 prefs on the ood failures while fixing all their hard violations.

Kept the parent's single native call (its event set/state tracking is good) and added a zero-token repair tool. Overlap is 47/58 dev_in, 42/63 dev_v2 and 19/43 ood failures, almost all on turns that only add or move ONE event while the previous calendar was already valid. The tool returns the LLM answer untouched when valid; otherwise it re-derives hard constraints by regex from user messages (event-id or name match, 'finish by X' = end<=X, soft 'ideally' sentences ignored), treats previous-calendar positions as known-legal anchors and moves the fewest events, nearest to the LLM's spot. Chit-chat turns with no JSON list (no_json) fall back to the previous calendar. Unlike the failed extract-then-solve children, the LLM never has to restate the whole constraint set.

Same single native call; repair tool rewritten. Evidence: 4 dev_in fails are the LLM silently shrinking durations (now locked to the previous calendar unless the user resizes), 5 dev_v2 fails are 'revert to Turn N' keeping later events (now rebuilt from that turn's calendar, constraints only from turns<=N), several overlaps were returned untouched because misparsed constraints made the search infeasible (now degrades through relaxed constraint sets instead of emitting an overlap), 'for a 12:30 pm slot' was not parsed, and LLM-moved events with unknown constraints now prefer their previous legal spot. Soft preferences (ood soft_mean 0.65, 11 soft misses, several caused by repair itself moving events out of the preferred window) are now parsed with a general day-part lexicon + soft time expressions and optimised in the same min-move search (pref penalty ~2 moves, unknown-constraint events pinned).

Child 1's repair tool (duration lock, revert-to-Turn-N rebuild, infeasibility fallback, prev-position anchoring, preference-aware min-move search) plus a zero-extra-call generalisation hook: the single assistant call also appends a 'PREFS:' JSON list in a generic schema (window / avoid / order / adjacent / gap). The tool uses the deterministic day-part lexicon first and the LLM's PREFS for events/relations the lexicon misses, so unseen preference types in future evaluation can still be optimised. Motivated by ood soft_mean 0.65 and the instruction to prefer general mechanisms over hard-coded phrase lists.

Child 1's repair tool (duration lock, revert-to-Turn-N rebuild, infeasibility fallback, prev-position anchoring, preference-aware min-move search) plus a dedicated non-thinking preference-extractor role that writes generic preference JSON (window / avoid / order / adjacent / gap) for the tool to optimise. Keeps the main assistant prompt untouched (no risk to its hard accuracy) and tests whether a separate cheap extraction call generalises to unseen preference phrasing better than the lexicon alone; costs one extra short call. Motivated by ood soft_mean 0.65 with 11 soft misses.

Tool-only fix, same single LLM call. In most hard failures (train-85, train-930, v2-1254/272/8450, oodA-3781) the LLM had placed the event legally and repair overrode it: 'from 11 to 1pm' was parsed as 'at 1pm', 'later than/past/onwards/earlier than/prior to' and bare hours were missed, and a stale previous calendar (later assistant turns without JSON) was trusted as legal. Repair now parses those phrasings, drops old-turn constraints that both the previous calendar and the LLM violate (misparse), treats a stale calendar as untrusted, tracks deletions across all turns since that calendar (v2-4990 extra event), stems name matching ('Outcome'~'Outcomes'), and uses an exact order-based packing search for feasibility and as fallback instead of returning an overlap (train-1005).

Different trust hypothesis: repair stops pulling unknown-constraint events back to their previous slot (TRUST_LLM) - in v2-8450, v2-1254, oodA-3781 and oodA-2559 that pull replaced a correct LLM placement with an illegal or preference-missing one - and instead gets constraint knowledge from a cheap CONS line the LLM appends (no PREFS line, fewer tokens than c2). Includes all of child 1's parsing/stale-calendar/deletion/packing-fallback fixes, so repair still only moves events that provably conflict.

Child 1's repair fixes (constraint phrasings, misparse check against previous calendar + LLM, stale-calendar handling, cross-turn deletions, exact packing fallback) plus the LLM now appends a CONS line (per-event constraint) and a generic PREFS line. Evidence: every hard failure involved repair not knowing or misreading a constraint (e.g. oodA-3781 event 0 'after 2:45pm' unknown, moved to 14:15); CONS fills unknown constraints and arbitrates regex/LLM disagreements by which one the LLM's own placement satisfies. PREFS (window/avoid/order/adjacent/gap) lets the existing preference optimiser handle preference types the regex lexicon has never seen, at ~200 extra output tokens.

Cheap tool-only fix, same single LLM call. In train-94 and v2-7041 the LLM output every event but repair dropped one (missing_event): an earlier deletion sentence matched to the wrong event by name was treated as authoritative. Now an event the LLM kept is only dropped when its deletion named the explicit event id. PREF_PEN is raised 2.1->2.6 because in oodA-801 and oodA-1771 both preferences could be met by moving about two events with known constraints, but the min-move search ranked that just below one unmet preference.

The LLM now appends a CONS list of every event's hard constraint and repair reads it (USE_LLM_CONS on; only the first list after CONS is read). In 4 of 6 hard failures (train-1005, oodA-3781, v2-1254, v2-272) the LLM had the event legal but overlapping, and repair, which could not regex-parse that event's old constraint, moved it into an illegal slot. v2-1254 and v2-272 are fully packed days (360/360 min), where repacking without every constraint is guesswork. Also includes the c1 fix that stops repair dropping an LLM-kept event on a name-matched deletion (train-94, v2-7041).

Structural: the LLM first writes CONS (every event's hard constraint) and PREFS (soft wishes in a generic window/avoid/order/adjacent/gap schema), then the calendar. Repair uses both (USE_LLM_CONS on; only typed entries of the first PREFS list are read) so it no longer moves events with regex-invisible old constraints into illegal slots (train-1005, oodA-3781, v2-1254, v2-272), and handles unseen preference types through the generic schema instead of the regex lexicon. Planning first should also reduce the LLM's own overlaps. Includes the c1 fixes: PREF_PEN 2.6 (oodA-801/1771) and no name-matched drop of LLM-kept events (train-94, v2-7041).

Tool-only; targets hard fails where repair pushed an event of unparsed constraint into an illegal slot (oodA-3781 0@14:15 vs after 2:45pm, v2-1254, v2-272, train-1005). Every at/before/after/between constraint is an interval of legal starts, so any start between two gold-history starts of the same event and duration is legal. Moves inside that hull now cost 1.0, inside the hull extended to the LLM's spot 1.5, and outside 2.3. Add sentences that still mention a time no longer mark the event as unconstrained, so the hull covers them (reproduced oodA-3781: 0 now goes to 15:30).

Union of c1 and c2, plus pronoun coreference, still one LLM call. Hard side: the legal-hull move cost for unknown-constraint events (oodA-3781, v2-1254, v2-272), and add sentences that mention a time stay unknown. A sentence starting with it/this/the meeting now takes its constraint from the event named in the previous sentence ('Add X (event id: 7). It needs to wrap up by 2pm.'). Soft side: cheap moves for new and validated-known events, plus pref_pack exact re-packing with preference windows as bounds (oodA-1871, -3110, -195, -1771).

Tool-only, same single LLM call; targets the preference misses (oodA-1871, -3110, -195, -1771). The grader ignores moves, so moving a new event (0.15) or an old event whose parsed constraint its previous slot satisfies (0.25) is now cheap next to an unmet preference (2.6); unknown-constraint events still cost 1.5. A new pref_pack pass re-packs known events exactly with preference windows as hard bounds, because the edge-aligned min-move search missed chained rearrangements (reproduced the oodA-1871 shape). Add sentences that still mention a time (an unparsed constraint) now leave the event unknown instead of 'known unconstrained'.

Tool-only change, same single LLM call. 3 of 4 hard fails (train-1005, v2-1254, v2-272) are fully packed 360-min days where repair shifts an event with an unparsed constraint the wrong way, and oodA-3781 is the same tie (14:15 vs 15:30). For such events the repair now reads direction words (after/no earlier/... vs before/by/wrap up/...) in the sentences about them and adds a safe one-sided bound at the edge of their known-legal hull, and moving them costs more the farther they leave the hull. Also: spoken times are rewritten into clock form (half past 2, quarter to 3, 3 in the afternoon, 4 o'clock), names match on 5-letter prefixes (v2-4990 'Outcome Analysis' did not match 'Analyzing ... Outcomes'), and an event the LLM brings back after it was deleted earlier is dropped unless the user asked for it (v2-4990 extra event).

Conservative hard side plus a general soft channel. The repair gets only the low-risk parts of child 1: spoken-time rewriting, 5-letter-prefix name matching (v2-4990 'Outcome Analysis'), dropping deleted events the LLM resurrects (v2-4990 extra event), and a distance-from-legal-hull cost so unknown-constraint events on fully packed days (v2-1254 moved 14:00->11:30) shift as little as possible. No direction inference. The LLM appends a typed PREFS line (window/avoid/order/adjacent/gap) that the repair optimises, so preference types not seen yet are covered by a general mechanism instead of the regex lexicon alone.

Child 1's repair (direction-word bounds for unparsed constraints on packed days, spoken-time rewriting, 5-letter-prefix name match, drop resurrected deleted events), plus the LLM now appends CONS and PREFS JSON lines that the repair already knows how to read (USE_LLM_CONS on). The hard fails in train-1005, v2-1254, v2-272 and oodA-3781 all come from constraints the regex could not parse, so the LLM's reading fills those in, and only where it agrees with the known-legal positions. PREFS adds a general typed preference channel (window/avoid/order/adjacent/gap) for preference types not yet seen, at ~150 extra output tokens.

Abbreviation-safe sentence splitting (as in c1, fixes the lost 'Dr. Patel' preference in oodA-1771), plus a costlier move for events whose constraint repair cannot see. All 3 hard fails (train-1005, v2-1254, v2-272) are 360-minute packed days. In each one the LLM's spot for the unknown-constraint event was legal, and repair carried that event 25-150 min outside both its history hull and the LLM's spot (event 0 10:45->12:30, event 2 14:00->11:30, event 0 12:00->11:35). Leaving the LLM-widened hull now costs 1.8 (was 1.3) plus 1/75 per minute beyond it, so the search shifts known-constraint and new events instead.

Single cheap tool fix, same one LLM call. In oodA-1771 the preference 'Ideally the "weekly research sync with Dr. Patel" event (event id: 0) happens toward the end of my day' was cut at 'Dr.' by the sentence splitter, so the half holding the event id had no wish word and the preference was lost (event 0 stayed at 10:00). The splitter now keeps abbreviations (Dr., Mr., Prof., St., e.g., single initials) inside their sentence. The same bug can also detach hard constraints from their event id in history messages, which leaves those events' constraints unknown to the repair search.

Structural/representation change on the same single LLM call. All 3 hard fails (train-1005, v2-1254, v2-272) are packed days where repair moved an event whose constraint its regex could not parse, and moved it in the wrong direction. The LLM is now asked to append a CONS list (the hard constraint of every event) and a PREFS list (generic window/avoid/order/adjacent/gap wishes, for preference types not seen yet), and repair's existing USE_LLM_CONS path is switched on. That path uses an LLM constraint only for events whose constraint regex could not parse, or when the LLM's spot satisfies it while the regex reading is broken in both spots. Also includes the abbreviation-safe sentence splitter that fixes oodA-1771's lost 'Dr. Patel' preference.

Repair-only change. In both hard fails (train-1005, v2train-272) repair moved old events whose constraint it could not see far outside every slot they had ever held (event 0 10:45->12:30, event 0 12:00->11:35), and in train-1005 it even replaced a fully valid LLM calendar; the soft DIST_OUT penalty from gen07 did not stop this. New search order: first a STRICT pass where such events may only sit inside their known-legal hull widened by the LLM's spot; then strict with old-message constraints that the LLM's full-history answer violates treated as misparses; only then the old free search.

Aggressive token cut plus the c1 repair fix. The LLM no longer sees old turns at all: a brief tool gives it the latest calendar annotated with each event's time rule (parsed by repair's own regex; unparsed ones say 'keep its current time'), the revert-target calendar if any, and only the new user message(s). Repair still reads the full native history, keeps constraint-unknown events at known-legal slots, and gets the strict-hull first pass from c1 (train-1005, v2train-272). Tests whether the LLM's job can be shrunk to applying one edit, at well under half the tokens.

Token cut plus the c1 repair fix. ~3k tokens/sample (0.015 fitness) are mostly re-sent old calendars; the parent's failures are all repair-side, not LLM-understanding errors, and repair re-reads the full native history itself. A brief tool keeps every user message verbatim but only the latest (and any revert-target) calendar, and the LLM runs in transcript mode on that brief. Repair gets the strict-hull first pass from c1 (train-1005, v2train-272).

Turns on the dormant LLM-constraint channel (USE_LLM_CONS=True) and asks the assistant to append CONS (per-event hard rule in the dataset's canonical form) and generic PREFS lines. Every parent failure traces to a constraint repair's regex could not see: hard fails train-1005 (event 0 'before 11:45am') and v2-272 (event 0 'between 12pm and 1:45pm') were carried out of range as unknown-constraint events, and soft misses oodA-195/oodA-3110 were feasible but blocked because moving unknown events (e.g. 3110 event 5 'after 11:45am') costs more than a missed preference. The existing conservative merge only fills regex gaps with LLM rules that the LLM's or previous slot satisfies; PREFS adds order/adjacent/gap/avoid wishes for unseen preference types.

Same CONS/PREFS assistant prompt as c1, but repair trusts the LLM's reading more. (a) LLM says null and no user sentence about the event carries any time hint -> the event counts as known-free (cheap to move), not unknown. (b) A regex rule that history contradicts (the 'misparsed' set) is replaced by the LLM's rule when the previous slot satisfies it, instead of leaving the event unknown. Motivation: in oodA-195/oodA-3110 the preferred layout was feasible but needed moves of events repair treated as unknown, and both hard fails (train-1005, v2-272) were unknown-constraint events pushed out of range.

Structural variant: a small dedicated constraint reader instead of changing the assistant prompt (which stays empty, so its calendar quality cannot regress). A brief tool reuses repair's regex and sends the cons LLM only the events it cannot parse, plus the user messages mentioning them and the last message; the LLM returns their hard rules (CONS) and generic soft wishes (PREFS). Repair turns on USE_LLM_CONS (conservative merge) and also reads PREFS from it. Evidence: all four parent failures were unknown-constraint events (hard fails train-1005, v2-272 pushed out of range; soft misses oodA-195, oodA-3110 blocked because moving unknown events costs more than a missed preference).

Same router as c1 but broader routing, to save tokens on ood too. Also short-path: (a) wishes about any event that repair's own lexicon reads (e.g. oodA-195 'event 2 around midday', oodA-3110 'toward the end of my day'), since repair decides those placements anyway; (b) adds whose hard rule the regex cannot parse, where the short prompt also asks the LLM for that one rule in canonical form ('before 2pm' ...), read from the new message alone and applied only to the new event. This differs from gen08a2's CONS channel, which rewrote rules for old events and hurt ood. Relational or unseen wish types still go to the full-history path.

Router for token cost (3.1k tok/sample = -0.016 fitness; all 4 parent failures are repair-side, not LLM-side). One tool file plays two roles: as 'brief' (no assistant key yet) it classifies the last turn; a pure add (one new event id, one duration, no edit/delete/revert words, timing rule the regex parses or no timing, no wish/relational sentence) gets a ~100-token prompt asking only for the new event's title, and repair builds the answer from the gold previous calendar + the new event. Every other turn (all ood wish turns, edits, unparsed rules) gets the full conversation verbatim in transcript form, so the LLM sees what native mode showed. Unlike gen08a1_c2/c3, compression never touches turns where the LLM's reading matters.

c1's strict router plus compression on the complex path only: there, old assistant calendars are replaced by a one-line stub except the latest and any revert target, while all user messages stay verbatim. gen08a1_c2 applied this compression to every turn and lost 0.02 on ood_dev (n=50, about one hard fail, possibly noise). Here pure adds take the short path, and repair still reads the full native history for hulls and constraints, so the compression only affects edit and wish turns.

Child 1's preference fix plus a token cut. On the complex path the brief swaps the stock 9-rule SYSTEM prompt (~450 tokens, repeated in every complex sample) for a ~150-token restatement that keeps the before/after/at/between semantics, the 10:00-16:00 window and the no-overlap rule, and keeps any rule 10+ verbatim. Repair enforces those rules anyway, and tokens cost about 0.01 of fitness at ~2.1k tokens per sample, so this should save about 0.0015 without touching accuracy.

Repair-only fix for the 4 ood_dev soft misses. The first solve attempt pinned every unknown-constraint event to its old slot, including the events the user had just attached a wish to (oodA-1486: event 5 stayed at 11:15 next to a free 11:30 slot; oodA-1177, oodA-195 and oodA-3110 were similar). Wished-for events are now exempt from the pin and from pref_pack's freeze, and moving one into its own wished window costs 1.0 instead of 1.5 plus distance. Prompts and topology are unchanged. Simulated replays of 1486, 195 and 3110 now meet every preference.

Child 1's preference fix plus an LLM read of hard rules the regex cannot parse. Both hard fails (train-1005, v2-272) were packed days where repair moved an event whose rule it could not read off its legal LLM slot. On complex turns the brief now lists those event ids and asks the assistant to append 'CONS: [...]' for them only, and repair turns on USE_LLM_CONS so the existing merge logic adopts a rule when the LLM's own placement satisfies it. A simulated v2-272 replay goes from event 0 at 11:35 (illegal) to 12:30 (legal).

Same seeded-search fix as c1, plus two parsing and routing generalisations. (1) Clock times written as words ('half past two', 'two thirty', 'by four', 'between two and four', 'quarter to two') are rewritten to digits before parsing; the regex could not read them, and unknown constraints are what make repair move events the wrong way (v2-272's 11:35 output matches an unparsed 'between 12pm and 1:45pm'). (2) When the turns after the latest calendar are only small talk (no ids, edit/add/delete words, durations or time words), that calendar is treated as current: pure adds take the cheap title-only route and repair keeps its known-legal anchors and hulls instead of the 'stale' mode.

Repair-search robustness fix. Both hard failures (train-1005, v2train-272) are zero-slack days (durations sum to 360 min). Replaying train-1005 with every constraint parsed, the min-move search used 48 s without finishing and the loop then fell back to a nearly unconstrained attempt, which broke two constraints. oodA-3110's real output also matches the parent's no-preference fallback. The exact packer's feasible placement, settled toward the LLM/previous slots, is now the branch-and-bound seed and the guaranteed answer for every unpinned attempt, so a proven-feasible constraint set is never relaxed. Budgets were cut from 50/20/8 s to 40/12/6 s. In replays the zero-slack cases with known constraints pass and finish in about 12 s instead of 48 s.

Same seeded-search fix as c1, plus a token-cost hypothesis. The brief replaces the standard nine-rule SYSTEM prompt with an equivalent compact rule list (~140 fewer tokens; any rule 10+ is kept verbatim) and appends /no_think to complex (non-pure-add) turns. Accuracy depends mostly on the deterministic repair role, which re-derives constraints and timing, while the LLM only needs to supply the event set, names and durations. At lambda=0.005 every 1k tokens saved is worth 0.005 fitness.
